idea: Paid newsletter on the economics of the built environment
pain: Nobody writes about buildings and money in the same place
v1: A weekly essay with real numbers
verdict: Her most natural voice and a genuine editorial gap, but the retail newsletter arithmetic does not work.

why.distribution: From a standing start with no list; the audience must be built entirely from zero.
why.demand: Inferred; the gap is real but nobody has asked to pay for it.
why.fmf: The intersection is her actual life, and the writing would be genuinely distinctive.
why.defensibility: Voice and back catalogue at a genuine intersection; hard to imitate credibly.
why.tailwind: Real interest in housing, infrastructure and cities, though attention is fragmenting.
why.ceiling: £20/mo x 960 subscribers = £230k gross, needing an audience of roughly 20,000.

ceiling_arithmetic: £20/mo x 960 paying x 87% after platform fees = £200k. At 5% conversion that needs ~19,000 free subscribers within twelve months from zero. Realistic year one: 100-250 paying = £21-52k.
carries: The most authentic thing she could write, at an intersection genuinely nobody occupies.
kills: Retail newsletter arithmetic. At £20/month the subscriber count required is unreachable in a year from zero.
test: Write six essays publicly and measure whether strangers - not friends - subscribe.
test_pass: Organic growth from outside her network.
test_fail: Readership plateaus at people she knows.
